Android's Qualcomm Wi-Fi Display stack casts the desktop to a TV. The root tool is `rungic-cast` (`shared/android/rungic-cast`, `/data/adb/rungic-wfd`). The Rungic app runs it for `op: cast` requests.

The transport uses the platform socket, `$RUNGIC_PLATFORM_SOCKET`. Each direction sends one JSON object per line. Each connection carries one request. A cast request may take a minute. Connecting may take three minutes. Changing resolution may take five and a half minutes.

The Linux consumer is `desktop/cast/rungic-cast`. The cast quick setting and `rungic-cast-watch` use it. It first queries platform status. If the app does not answer because it is asleep, the consumer reports `host-unreachable`. It then sends {op: cast, args: [command, argument]}.

The `status` and `capabilities` commands return the same object. Its fields are `protocol_version`, `active_state`, `active`, `reconnecting`, `receivers` and `displays`. Protocol version is 1. The consumer reports `backend-incompatible` for another version or if `receivers` is not a list.

Each receiver represents one TV. An `active_state` of 2 means connected. `active` is the connected TV or null. The quick setting reads `active_state`, `active.name` and `reconnecting`.

Errors use {"error": string, "code": string}. Code `component-missing` means the tool is not installed. The commands `scan`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `resolution` and `settings` change Android state or its displayed interface. The provider check never sends them.

`tools/tests/test_contract_wifi_display.py` checks the real consumer against the substitute in `tools/contracts.py`. Acceptance scenario `contract.wifi-display` checks the app and tool on the phone. That check blanks TV names and addresses on the phone.
